method_notes: Brent Admission Arrangements for Community Schools 2026/27 ('Tie-break' Distance Measurement, p5): distance measured in a straight line from the address point in the property to the address point in the school, as determined by Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG) data, using the measuring module of The Access Group admissions software (Ordnance Survey maps + LLPG, accurate to 1 cm); the arrangements also publish grid-reference measuring points (easting/northing) for each community school (p2). Nearer applicants have priority; where children are equidistant for the last place, computerised random allocation. The Sept 2027 primary handbook repeats straight-line measurement 'from a point in the property to a point in the school'. Exceptions in school entries in the handbook: Kilburn Grange (free school) uses the shortest walking route to the school's main entrance point; East Lane and Preston Manor measure from the front door of the home to school reception; NWL Jewish Day School to the main gate (straight line); Ark Franklin gives priority to Pupil Premium children within a 0.5-mile radius. Council tables give furthest distance per criterion in metres; furthest distance is not shown for looked-after, social/medical, pupil premium, staff children or 'nearest school with a vacancy' (directed) offers.

gaps: All three years come from the council's own 'How places were offered - Reception' PDFs (2024, 2025, 2026), which give furthest distance per oversubscription criterion in metres, plus an Over/Under/Fully subscribed flag. Interpretation: schools flagged 'Undersubscribed' (and Northview 2026, 'Fully subscribed' but filled with directed 'nearest school with a vacancy' offers) are recorded as all_offered, with the furthest distance noted in criterion_note; for oversubscribed/fully subscribed schools the value is the furthest distance in the last-priority criterion with a distance. That is the furthest offer within that criterion, not necessarily the strict cut-off. The 2024 table lists criteria alphabetically within each school, not in priority order, so the general criterion (Any Other Applicant/Distance/Outside Catchment Area) was chosen; for Islamia, Princess Frederica and St Joseph's RC Infant the last faith/parish criterion was chosen by hand by matching the 2025-26 ordering. Those three 2024 values are inferences. 2024 table has no PAN or application counts; PAN is taken from the 2026 table (Harris South Kenton shows 150 as printed). Faith schools (Avigdor Hirsch, Islamia, NWLJDS, Sinai, St Joseph's RC Infant/Primary, Princess Frederica, St Robert Southwell 2025) often filled on faith criteria; their distances are flagged in criterion_note and are not general proximity cut-offs. Measuring method for academies/VA/free schools taken only from the short criteria summaries in the Sept 2027 handbook; where it says nothing, straight line (the LA method) is assumed and not verified against each school's full policy. Only Kilburn Grange is known to use a walking route. Byron Court Primary closed Aug 2024; its 2024 figures are attributed to Harris Primary Academy South Kenton (same site). Malorees Infant figures (2024-25) are attributed to Malorees Primary (renamed 2026). Leopold's two 2024 sites are merged into one entry. Barham 2026 'Any Other Applicant' furthest distance printed as 999999 (placeholder), irrelevant as the school was undersubscribed. Junior schools (Mount Stewart Jr, Roe Green Jr, St Joseph's Catholic Jr, St Mary Magdalen's Jr, Our Lady of Grace Jr, Kilburn Park Foundation) excluded. Postcodes and types from GIAS (Oct 2026 extract), not the booklet. All documents were fetched with plain curl from brent.gov.uk; no blocking encountered.
